currentContext.business: Batliboi manufactures, engineers, contracts and markets advanced machinery from plants in Surat (India) and Peterborough (Canada), with product designs developed in-house or in collaboration with leading engineering companies worldwide. Its operations span the Machine Tool Group (CNC and conventional metal-cutting/metal-forming machines, plus an agency-house trading business representing overseas principals), the Textile Engineering Group (Air Engineering humidification and waste-collection plant, and Textile Machinery for spinning, knitting and processing), and the Environmental Engineering Group (air pollution control equipment, industrial fans and green hydrogen projects). Customers are served through corporate-level Business Groups backed by a dedicated engineering team providing pre-sales and post-sales service via a network of multiple offices across the country.

Machine Tool Group: Traded metal cutting and metal forming machine tools (agency house for overseas principals)
Air Engineering Group: Auto control type humidification plant equipment
Automatic controls for textile spinning, weaving and knitting plants
Air control solutions for food, pharmaceuticals and general industry
Quickmill Inc., Canada (subsidiary): Large size Gantry Drilling & Milling machines

currentContext.strengths: Long-standing franchise: incorporated in 1941 and described as a leader among engineering companies, with 82 years of continuity as a listed engineering house|Technology access through both in-house development and collaboration with leading engineering companies worldwide|Agency-house model representing reputed overseas principals from Czech Republic, Belgium, Italy, Germany, South Korea, China and Taiwan alongside own manufactured machines|Turnkey project capability as engineers and contractors, executed both in India and internationally|Nationwide pre-sales and post-sales service through a dedicated engineering team and a network of multiple offices across the country|EEG has in-house capabilities of providing 100% Make in India solutions across steel, power, oil & gas, sugar, cement and solar manufacturing industries|Textile Machinery Group retained overall market share and average business volume despite high demand and raw-material price volatility, via product portfolio expansion and wider geographic reach through key representations|Machine Tool Manufacturing improved market share on the back of better quality and more new CNC models|Cordial and pro-active industrial relations with employees at all levels including the union
currentContext.strategies: Use the Employee Stock Option Plan as a retention and alignment tool: after a long gap, three fresh grant lots (10th, 11th and 12th) were made in FY2025-26 to divisional and functional leadership across Machine Tool Manufacturing and Foundry, Machine Tool Trading, Air Engineering, Textile Machinery, Environmental Engineering and corporate finance, with options vesting in three instalments after 36, 48 and 60 months from grant.|Maintain an annual, externally validated safety and compliance discipline - safety audit conducted once a year by an independent consultant as a matter of Company practice, alongside an equal-opportunity workplace policy covering permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees.|Run a proactive, framework-based risk management approach in which risks in the internal and external environment are assessed, monitored, evaluated and mitigated rather than handled reactively.|Dividend is recommended annually by the Board on both equity and preference capital and is paid only after approval by members at the Annual General Meeting; for the year under review a final equity dividend plus the contracted 1% and 8% preference dividends were recommended subject to that approval. The year's result is taken directly to Retained Earnings rather than appropriated to a separate reserve. Share issuance is kept narrow and purpose-bound: during the year equity and preference shares were issued only to give effect to the NCLT-sanctioned Scheme of Amalgamation of Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited, and equity was issued on exercise of employee stock options; apart from these, no shares with differential rights as to dividend or voting, and no sweat equity shares, were issued. Employee ownership is used as a deliberate retention lever - the Company operates an Employee Stock Option Plan approved by members in December 2011 with a view to encourage, reward and retain employees and to give them an opportunity to participate in the growth of the Company, administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, which also grants the options. The Company maintains an active investor-servicing discipline, including measures to reduce the quantum of unclaimed dividends and to ensure timely receipt of dividend warrants by shareholders.|Annual independent safety audit: as a matter of Company practice a safety audit is conducted once a year, and for the year under review it was conducted by an Independent Consultant.|Prevention of sexual harassment: a POSH policy covering all permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees is in place with a constituted Internal Complaint Committee, and the policy is published on the Company's website; no complaints were received during 2025-2026 and none were pending for more than 90 days.|Equal-opportunity workplace: the Company states it is an equal opportunity employer and consciously strives to build a work culture that promotes the dignity of all employees.|Maternity benefit compliance: the Company has complied with the provisions relating to the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended from time to time.|Board-level risk management framework: an adequate risk management framework capable of addressing risks is in place, under which risks in the internal and external environment are assessed, monitored, evaluated and mitigated proactively.|Internal financial control: the Audit Committee has established and maintained an effective Internal Control over financial reporting, with standard operating practices laid down, followed and independently audited.|Clean audit and fraud record: the statutory audit report for 2025-2026 contains no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and no frauds were reported by the statutory auditors under Section 143(12).|Unclaimed dividend stewardship: as on 31st March 2026 the Company had no unpaid dividend due for transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund, and the list of dividends previously transferred to IEPF is published on the Company's website.|Environmental engineering as a business line: the group's subsidiary Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited is engaged in Water Effluent Treatment Plant and Zero Liquid Discharge solutions for industries, aligning a revenue stream with industrial water-pollution abatement.
currentContext.expansion: Batliboi's FY2025-26 expansion effort was concentrated at the Udhna manufacturing facilities and in energy self-sufficiency. Capital expenditure in the foundry and machine shop was completed during FY25-26 with the aim of increasing production, improving productivity and quality and reducing cost; combined with ongoing redesign and modification of machines based on customer and competitive feedback, this resulted in production rising by around 30% compared with the prior fiscal. In the foundry, a new energy-efficient induction furnace of 6T capacity was commissioned, delivering power savings of about 21%. On renewable self-generation, installation of an 800 kW roof-top solar plant is underway and will be commissioned in the first quarter of FY26-27, and the Company plans to add a further 400 kW of solar in FY26-27; combined savings from solar and the existing windmill are expected to reduce power cost, and LED lighting continues to be rolled out through the shop and assembly areas as an ongoing process. The product basket is being widened through design-stage work on a smaller version of the Vertical Turning Lathe and a large-size Vertical Machining Center, while the Air Engineering Group has completed a set of shop-floor and product improvements (new geared motor and door for the screen filter, new impellers for semi-central units, a dust-proof area for finished goods, a dock leveler for export container loading and epoxy flooring for the shop). At the Canadian subsidiary Quickmill, High Rail machine development continues and development of a new HD Rail machine has started. Structurally, the Scheme of Amalgamation merging Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited with and into Batliboi Limited was given effect during the year following the NCLT Mumbai order, with equity shares allotted on 24th June 2025 and 8% redeemable preference shares on 23rd March 2026 to the transferor company's shareholders.
currentContext.mdna: Management identifies global and domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices of finished goods as a primary swing factor for the Company's operations.|Input availability and input prices are flagged as a key influence on operations.|Changes in government regulations and tax laws, and economic developments in India and in the countries in which the Company conducts business, are called out as drivers of variance versus forward-looking statements.|Litigation and industrial relations are named among the incidental factors that could influence operations.

risks.risk: Global and domestic demand-supply swings that move selling prices of finished goods
risks.note: The Board's cautionary statement names demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices of finished goods as the first factor that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements - for a capital-goods maker with no pricing power over cyclical customer capex, this is the primary earnings swing factor.

Explicitly flagged in the cautionary statement; the Company converts bought-out material and components into machinery, so availability gaps or price spikes compress margins between order booking and execution.

risks.risk: Changes in government regulations and tax laws
risks.note: Named as a factor that could influence operations. The year already carried a concrete instance of this exposure: the exceptional item mainly comprised a non-cash charge due to the introduction of the New Labour Code.

risks.risk: Economic and political developments in the overseas markets where the Company operates
risks.note: The cautionary statement covers economic developments in India and in countries in which the Company conducts business; the Company runs a manufacturing subsidiary in Peterborough, Canada (Quickmill Inc.) selling globally into Energy, Heat Transfer, Steel Service, large industrial machinery and job shop sectors, so a meaningful share of the consolidated business is exposed to non-Indian cycles and currency.

Listed among the factors that could influence operations. As at the reporting date, however, no significant or material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals affecting going-concern status, and no application has been made under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.

Named in the cautionary statement as an incidental factor that could influence operations; the Company runs unionised manufacturing facilities, so a breakdown in industrial relations would directly interrupt production.

risks.risk: Concentration of consolidated earnings in subsidiaries outside the standalone entity
risks.note: The Directors' Report shows the standalone entity in loss before tax for the year while the consolidated result stayed in profit, meaning subsidiary operations - Quickmill Inc., Canada and the newly incorporated Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited - carry a disproportionate share of group profitability and any setback there would be felt directly.

risks.risk: Execution risk in a newly incorporated business line
risks.note: Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech Private Limited was only incorporated in April 2025 and is engaged in Water Effluent Treatment Plant and Zero Liquid Discharge work for industries - an unproven vertical whose track record is a single part year.

one-line thesis: Batliboi closed FY26 with a record order backlog of INR 593 Cr (+75% YoY) and INR 990 Cr inflows, signaling strong FY27 revenue visibility despite FY26 PAT being suppressed to INR 7 Cr by one-time labor code provisions and merger accounting. The strategic pivot toward high-margin environmental engineering (ZLD/Green Hydrogen) and expanded CNC product baskets offers a clear path to operating leverage and margin expansion beyond the current ~7% levels.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 440 Cr (+7% YoY); EBITDA Margin: Stable (~7-8%) despite supply chain headwinds; PAT: INR 7 Cr (impacted by one-time labor code provisioning and BEEL merger accounting distortions); Order Book: INR 593 Cr (vs INR 339 Cr prior year); Net Debt: Deleveraged to D/E 0.28x.
guidance: Revenue growth expected to accelerate in FY27 driven by record backlog; Margins expected to improve via volume leverage and operational efficiency (no major overhead expansion); Order inflow target to sustain >INR 900 Cr run-rate; Capex of INR 10 Cr planned for FY27 plus CAD 4 Mn (INR 25-30 Cr) for Canada expansion pending permits.
order book & pipeline: Total: INR 593 Cr. Breakdown: Textile Machinery (INR 238 Cr, 40%); Machine Tools (INR 163 Cr, 27%); Environmental Engineering (INR 32 Cr); Air Engineering (Balance). Inflow FY26: INR 990 Cr. Note: Backlog includes indirect sales (principal value) while revenue recognizes only commission on indirect, creating apparent mismatch.
segment / subsidiary detail: Machine Tools: Q4 inflow INR 60 Cr, installed 115 machines at Udhna. Quickmill (Canada): FY26 Rev INR 127 Cr, Q4 Rev INR 35 Cr, focusing on exports outside NA. Textile: FY26 Rev INR 50 Cr (Q4 INR 13 Cr), inflow INR 435 Cr. Environmental: Rev INR 35 Cr (Q4), inflow INR 17 Cr, focusing on ZLD and O&M. Air Engineering: FY26 Rev INR 57 Cr.
growth verticals / optionality: Green Hydrogen: MOU signed with L&T for Balance of Plant; MOU with Chinese manufacturer for electrolyzers; 2-3 active inquiries. ZLD: Targeting major projects in textile/process industries. CNC: Expanding from 2 platforms (Turning/VMC) to 4 by adding new designs annually. Canada: Plant expansion (CAD 4 Mn) awaiting municipal permits to unlock export capacity.
margins & cost dynamics: Current operating margin ~7% viewed as commoditized but expected to expand via volume leverage without proportional overhead increase. Fan division production capacity up 40%. Management cites continuous efficiency improvements via AI/IT tools and better tooling. One-time labor code provisions distorted FY26 bottom line.
capex / expansion: FY26 Cumulative: INR 27 Cr (primarily Machine Tools/Udhna). FY27 Planned: INR 10 Cr. Canada Expansion: CAD 4 Mn (INR 25-30 Cr) contingent on regulatory approvals in next 2 quarters.
capital allocation: Priority on deleveraging (achieved D/E 0.28x); Organic capex for capacity expansion (India & Canada); No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed in transcript but balance sheet strength supports potential returns.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical: Prolonged Middle East conflict impacting global economy/energy prices. Regulatory: Delays in Canada municipal permits for expansion. Sectoral: Textile industry cyclicality (though currently reviving). Execution: Conversion of Green Hydrogen MOUs to firm orders.
management quality / tone: Confident and forward-looking; Emphasizes 'best years ahead' despite macro headwinds; Defensive on margin queries citing continuous improvement; Transparent about one-time accounting hits; Aggressive on order book growth narrative.
non-obvious takeaways: Revenue/Backlog Mismatch: Backlog includes 100% value of indirect sales while revenue books only commission, artificially depressing asset turnover ratios if not adjusted. Export Safety: 100% of export receivables covered by Letters of Credit, nullifying Bangladesh geopolitical risk exposure. Fan Division: Hidden capacity jump of 40% not fully reflected in top-line yet due to mix.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
